subject: District Transportation Survey Development
overview: The subcommittee met to design a district-wide survey to assess student transportation needs and preferences before the current busing contract expires. Members discussed identifying barriers to student transit, evaluating late busing options for extracurricular activities, and addressing the impact of future high school construction on parking and bus demand.

items.title: Meeting Context and Purpose
items.summary: Chair Graham explained the need for a proactive survey to assess transportation facts and needs before the contract with Eastern Bus ends next school year. The goal is to use data to shape the next Request for Proposals and update outdated district policies.

items.title: Coordination with Safe Routes to School Survey
items.summary: The subcommittee discussed the recent launch of a state-run Safe Routes to School survey to ensure their efforts would not cause community confusion and to determine if they could access its raw data.

items.title: Survey Content Brainstorming
items.summary: Members brainstormed questions focusing on current modes of transport, reasons for satisfaction or dissatisfaction, and specific preferences between yellow buses and MBTA service. The discussion highlighted the need to gather data from both students and parents across all grade levels.

items.title: Operational Challenges and Driver Shortages
items.summary: Director Fidler-Carey detailed existing challenges with bus driver shortages, overcrowded routes, and enforcement of distance-based busing eligibility. Plans were discussed to encourage walking through neighborhood meetups and community education during the summer.

items.title: Late Busing and Extracurricular Access
items.summary: The subcommittee explored the potential for multi-tiered late busing to accommodate students participating in sports and after-school activities. Members noted that a lack of reliable transportation often prevents students from participating in school-sponsored programs.

items.title: Infrastructure and Future Planning Impacts
items.summary: Discussion addressed how upcoming high school construction might significantly reduce student parking, potentially increasing the demand for district-provided transportation. Members also reviewed how municipal decisions, such as the lack of protected bike lanes, influence student commuting choices.

items.title: Survey Timing and Outreach Strategy
items.summary: The group debated the best time to distribute the survey to ensure high and representative participation, considering a launch in early autumn or concurrent with spring bus registration. The subcommittee aims to present recommendations to the full School Committee by June.
